topic: Can new pigments still be discovered without claiming new human colors?

in_scope: computational prioritization and design-only validation planning
environmental and safety constraints at proposal level
out_of_scope: claiming a new fundamental color dimension

subhypotheses.statement: Undiscovered pigment candidates remain plausible in chemically and structurally diverse material spaces.
subhypotheses.allowed_conclusion: The candidate space is open; its remaining size is unknown.

subhypotheses.statement: Visual novelty requires a named reference library and stated viewing conditions.
subhypotheses.allowed_conclusion: Novelty must be operationalized as a protocol-dependent comparison.

subhypotheses.statement: Reflectance-spectrum novelty and CIE-coordinate novelty can diverge.
subhypotheses.allowed_conclusion: Both spectral and perceptual metrics must be retained.

subhypotheses.statement: Safety-constrained multiobjective ranking can efficiently prioritize candidates.
subhypotheses.allowed_conclusion: This is the proposed method, not an established pigment-discovery result.

evidence_sources.citation: Subramanian and Li, Materials Today Advances 16, 100323 (2022), doi:10.1016/j.mtadv.2022.100323
Buxbaum and Pfaff, Industrial Inorganic Pigments, 3rd ed. (2005)
Nassau, The Physics and Chemistry of Color, 2nd ed. (2001)
Curtarolo et al., Nature Materials 12, 191-201 (2013), doi:10.1038/nmat3568

evidence_limits: Publisher full text for S2 was CAPTCHA-protected during this run; unverified quantitative property values are excluded.
No pigment-specific open benchmark dataset was verified for the exact proposed materials family.
The plan has no observed experimental results.
